questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The employees of our company are not ______ of their freedom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. deprived.**

 
• deprive: **prevent **(a person or place) from having or using something.
 
• The given sentence talks about the employees not being **prevented** from their freedom, hence, deprive fits in the context of the given sentence, so, it will be used in the given blank.
 
• deny: state that one refuses to admit the truth or existence of.
 
• dissipate: disperse or scatter.
 
• deploy: move (troops or equipment) into position for military action.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the indirect form of the sentence.

A new student said to me, "Where is the Principal's office?"

options.text: A new student asked me where the Principal's office is.
A new student asked me where is the Principal's office.
A new student asked me where the Principal's office was.
A new student said to me where the Principal's office was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. a new student asked me where the Principal's office was.**

 
• when direct speech is in interrogation form **'said to'** is changed into **'asked'**.
 
• And the present tense of the sentence is also changed into the **past tense**.
 
• And the** interrogative sentence** is changed into the assertive sentence.
 
• All these rules are followed in option 3), hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

My grandmother has been lives in Shimla since her childhood days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. had been lives.**

 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect continuous tense**.
 
• And, in the present perfect continuous tense, **has/have+ been + V1+ing **is used.
 
• Hence, **has been living** will be used in the given sentence.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **My grandmother has been living in Shimla since her childhood days.**

questions.question:
**Choose the option that is the passive form of the sentence.**

The chief guest gave prizes to the children.

options.text: The children are given prizes by the chief guest.
The children were given prizes by the chief guest.
The children were being given prizes by the chief guest.
The children was given prizes by the chief guest.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• When changing active sentence to its passive form, subject and object interchange their places.
 
• Option 1 is wrong because the sentence is in the present tense but the given active sentence is in past tense. Tense remains the same in both sentences.
 
• Option 4 is wrong because the subject 'children' is in plural form so it is followed by the plural verb i.e. 'were'.
 
• Option 3 is wrong because 'being' is used while making the passive voice of continuous tenses but the given sentence is in past indefinite.
 
• **Therefore Option 2 'The children were given prizes by the chief guest' is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Then she does some gardening.

B. Finally before her mid morning nap, she eats a light breakfast.

C. My grandmother is an active eighty year old.

D. She begins her morning with meditation.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• The answer begins with sentence C as it is the introductory sentence. In all other remaining questions, there is a pronoun 'she/her' in which we do not know about the subject.
 
• The second sentence will be D because after introducing the grandmother, the sequence should be continued with her daily activities right from the morning.
 
• Sentence B will be the last sentence as we have the adverb 'finally'.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is followed by Option 2 i.e. 'CDAB'.**

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

Very little metals are as precious as gold.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• 'little' is used before uncountable nouns. Metals are countable therefore we use 'few/a few' in the given sentence.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is 'few/a few metals are as precious as gold.'**
